title: Bosch 605L Quad Door Refrigerator (KFN96VPEAA) $1389 (Price Check Button) + Delivery (~$59) @ The Good Guys
body:
Deal: Bosch 605L Quad Door Refrigerator (KFN96VPEAA) $1389 (Price Check Button) + Delivery (~$59) @ The Good Guys

[kampret] I just bought a Samsung fridge 3 months ago. Tempted to get this one, but I’m not sure how easy to sell a fridge on marketplace.
[hamza23] I don't use marketplace but my guess/prediction is that you would struggle to get a good price for your Samsung fridge, you are only selling to people in your local area and there might be some suspicions about the sale of a 3 month old fridge.
[seamonkey] Yes. What's your absolute lowest price? I can offer half of that if you can deliver to Fremantle tonight. I don't drive and I'm not actually home tonight, so you'll need to wait. It's for my son's birthday yesterday. Don't waste my time please, I'm a single parent.
[Jackson] @seamonkey: Hey, you are the bloke that asked if the iron I was selling was left handed, and when I said yes stopped responding
[wouldntpaythat] Hard sell. Your addressable market is limited to people with a ute or people who just happen to be moving with a truck booked.
Making it harder is working out if fridges fit. Pulling out measuring tape is too hard for some.
[JinXR] Samsung is garbage. Hope you get a decent offload price.
[Jackson] While I generally agree, I believe Samsung purchased Whirlpool International (not US) fridge manufacturing division, and they weren't half bad. Maybe someone can confirm?
[geremyfarr] I am looking for a new fridge and this seems good. Any experiences with the longevity. I've been super displeased with LG's french door models. I've had one for 4 years, and had to have the inverter replaced in that time, and frankly it still isn't functioning correctly.
Also wondering if it might be better to wait for Black Friday.
[Flintstone] Couldn't you get that fixed under warranty or ACL. 4 years is really fast for a fridge to die.
[geremyfarr] tell me about it. its just hard proving it has ongoing issues. the inverter was covered under warranty, but i think the technician who replaced it did something to the flow of cool air. As a result… bottom of the fridge items freeze and top/middle fridge seems hotter than normal.
Requires a call out fee and much much time. Also, "have you tried taking all the food out and letting it defrost for a full 24hrs + turn it back on and leave it empty for 24hrs" is not really freasible (see what i did there) as we don't have a second fridge.
[Roeroe] My Samsung fridge is going for 11 years now… Wonder if it is time for an upgrade…
[Click_It] You guys should all buy lotto tickets.
My experience is Samsung fridges and washing machines are all designed to die around warranty date.
[the1doood] They have older models which were stable.
[CharlieAus] Our samsung washing machine stopped working, a oddly long earth wire had broken, I replaced it and it's been going since. Same as fridge mentioned below, both bought about 13 years ago, would like to get new but both are working great still :(
[CharlieAus] Bought a 4 year old samsung double door fridge/freezer with ice and water 13~ years ago, it just won't die, I really want a new fridge but hard to justify it… It did freeze up a bit for a little while but I replaced the defrost element and it's been going great since.
[gooseberry] Damn, too tall for my current fridge alcove. Have to remove overhead cabinet - not sure worth it or look for another model that's shorter.
[kati] Same :(
Hardly any fridges out there that are less than 170cm tall!
[Bargainian] My Panasonic is going strong for 14 years. Thought of this as a backup but height of 1830mm is 20mm more than my fridge space.
But on the bright side, might get few more years from my Panasonic.
[Daniel Plainview] Plus really you need to factor in the recommended space around the sides, rear and top so that the heat exchange can occur efficiently - if you shoehorn a fridge into a space without it, it'll consume a lot more power and be much more noisy due to working harder to maintain temps.
[Jackson] For this reason a lot of above fridge cupboards are made shorter in depth so that there's always a cavity to vent heat out the back, if that was the case it would be fine to fit a fridge more tightly than usual
[morediscount] https://www.choice.com.au/home-and-living/kitchen/fridges/ar…
[donm] Wow. That's surprising. I generally consider Bosch products to be good quality.
[geremyfarr] I find this surprising if I'm honest. Some of their recommended fridges (including the one we currently have) have this issue, yet aren't reported. I'm getting a smidge worried about Choice's independence more recently. I think there is also a challenge for them providing year on year reviews that can't possibly speak to longevity.
[bargaineer] There are plenty of products they recommend that in real world use people despise.
Here is an example.
Choice - https://www.choice.com.au/products/home-and-living/kitchen/m…
ProductReview - https://www.productreview.com.au/listings/lg-ms2336db
[bargainhuntr] I wish I had not opened this link, their top of the list of not recommended fridge(Hisense) is the one I have…
Fortunately I have it for 9 months and haven't had a single issue yet.
The second on that list on not recommended fridge is this Bosch one. Which was my second choice while buying the fridge…boy can I pick them.
[silverwalker] oh shit, got the series 6 for 17xx, thought i got a good deal already, and this popped up…….
[Dmz111] It's a terrible deal. A fridge that can't stay cold
[andresampras] I bought this fridge over a year ago for $1700. As you’d hope it’s wayyyy better than our 10yo Kelvinator.
I like that the doors don’t have to be opened/closed in a particular order unlike others we checked out at the time. It’s quiet, and the veg drawers keep fruit and veg fresh WAY longer than our old fridge, was kinda freaky in the initial months of ownership. And the energy consumption is decent too. I also prefer the drawer setup in the freezer space, to me this is the most logical freezer setup for these freezer-at-bottom units, better than the shelves and much better than the one big drawer aka bottomless pit of unreachable anything.
Not sure about the Choice review, but my personal experience with this fridge has been all good
[ifreddo] A reviewer on the good guys site states you can't open the bottom left door without opening another door first. Is that true?
Somone also said to close the fridge door properly you have to push it quite hard?
[Wt133] I wouldn’t mind one but you need the alcove to be a specific space otherwise the door won’t open and my alcove is against a wall. I’m curious how many people buy one and find it don’t fit
[GGGGrrrrr] I get rid of 540-liter LG French-door refrigerator? It doesn’t even have any frost buildup yet. I bought it 2003.
I bought this fridge when my son was born, and it was still in perfect working order even after he graduated from Uni, so I’ve kept it in the garage and still only use it during the summer.
If I hadn’t bought the LG 910L French Door Fridge with a tinted finish last year through an acquaintance—for $499, which was 30% off the Second Factory price—I would still be using this one as my main fridge. I wanted to buy one with a larger capacity, but since 1.8 meters was the height limit, this model was the perfect fit.
[bargainhuntr] We had one in a shared rental I was living at before. Its just too good and spoils you. It was a Samsung model.
Contrary to all the negative press samsung get, The owner had it for 3 years and it was going smooth.
[Oofy Doofy] 2 doors and a draw has more space than 4 doors.
[yukey] Got this from Costco a year or two ago. The compressor could be very noisy, I once thought i might haven to send it to RMA. And the top beam of the 2 lower doors are very very hard to clean - they catch everything: debris, food scraps, broken veggie chips etc when you open the upper doors to get something. Won't vote for this design
[Jackson] May have considered this if it had a water dispenser
